A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Compression as Adaptation, and contain 27 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video representation, compression, inference-time scaling and editing experiments in Section 4 and Appendices B and F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative experiments and qualitative reconstruction/editing results in Section 4 and Appendices B and F.

M1.justification: The LoRA adaptation, one-vector hashing, entropy-constrained compression and importance-sampling refinement procedures are unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and the training procedure in Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Kodak images, UVG videos and HEVC B/C/E benchmarks, with unchanged reconstruction, compression, editing and prompt-variation scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain DCVC-RT, GLC-video, HM-RA and VTM-RA in Figure 4 and Appendix F. The removed Zhang et al. citation concerns background customization work, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain the same models, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets and inference settings. These include 832 × 480, 81-frame compression clips and the same scaling configurations in Table 3.

E4.justification: The rank/vector-size studies, scaling sweeps, early-stopping analyses and editing/irrelevant-prompt case studies are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The shared-PRNG discussion and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical curves, bitrate labels and qualitative outcomes match throughout Section 4 and Appendices B and F. No result entries, rankings or reported trends are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The diffusion/flow derivations, minimum-description-length argument, Proposition B.1 and proofs in Appendix D are unchanged. Citation-year updates do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about functional visual representations, compact adaptation vectors, perceptual compression and inference-time control. The broader visual-memory claim also remains.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 deletes the phrase describing adaptations as persistent visual memories, but retains the explanation that information persists and entities are remembered. Sections 4.4, B.4 and C.2 preserve this interpretation; mechanisms and limitations are otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, two-stage training procedure and editing instructions. The project website link and documented access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 and the bibliography remove Zhang et al. (2023), Composable LoRA for multi-concept customization of diffusion models. The He/RNE and Song references are publication updates to retained works; broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 receives a localized sentence shortening. Reference titles, venues and years, plus the arXiv version/date stamp, are updated. The main narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and legends are unchanged. Shortened prose causes local reflow on pages 5–6, and bibliography reflow moves the final reference from the right column to the left on page 12.

improvement.justification: v2 trims redundant wording, updates two references and removes one background citation. These localized editorial changes leave the scientific argument, empirical support, limitations and reproducibility information intact, without a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
